candidates.phrase: one true and living God, creator and Lord of heaven and earth
candidates.rationale: Conciliar confession directly names God as Lord of heaven and earth, affirming His sovereign authority.
candidates.chunk_text: The Holy, Catholic, Apostolic, and Roman Church believes and acknowledges that there is one true and living God, creator and Lord of heaven and earth, almighty, eternal, immeasurable, incomprehensible, infinite in understanding, will and every perfection. Since He is a one unique, completely simple and unchangeable spiritual substance, He must be declared to be, in reality and in essence, distinct from the world, supremely happy in and from Himself, and inexpressibly loftier than anything else which exists or can be imagined.

candidates.locator: Canon I.1 — De Deo Rerum Omnium Creatore
candidates.phrase: unum verum Deum visibilium et invisibilium Creatorem et Dominum
candidates.rationale: Canon affirms the one true God as Creator and Lord of all visible and invisible things, asserting divine lordship.
candidates.chunk_text: Si quis unum verum Deum visibilium et invisibilium Creatorem et Dominum negaverit; anathema sit.

candidates.phrase: He is the Lord of the universe, whose order he established
candidates.rationale: Catechism explicitly declares God (the almighty Father) to be Lord of the universe, affirming sovereign authority.
candidates.chunk_text: The Holy Scriptures repeatedly confess the universal power of God. He is called the "Mighty One of Jacob", the "LORD of hosts", the "strong and mighty" one. If God is almighty "in heaven and on earth", it is because he made them. Nothing is impossible with God, who disposes his works according to his will. He is the Lord of the universe, whose order he established and which remains wholly subject to him and at his disposal. He is master of history, governing hearts and events in keeping with his will: "It is always in your power to show great strength, and who can withstand the strength of your arm? "You are merciful to all, for you can do all thing"
